messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I sketched an 'Inspector' micro-panel for Console analytics. It would surface per-route routing policy, which model variant is in the fast lane, quota exposure, and sampling rate so folks can debug rollouts without digging through infra dashboards.
liam: Nice. UX question: do we show resolved model mapping (route -> model id + variant) and a small cost peek? e.g. est tokens/sec and cost per 1k?
maya: Yes, cost peek is useful. Minimal view: model_id, variant_tag, policy (latency/cost/region), quota_bucket, sampling_rate, estimated_cpm.
nina: API design debate: should this be embedded in savedview snapshots or a separate Inspector endpoint that savedviews point to? Embedding ensures snapshot fidelity, separate endpoint keeps savedview payloads small. :thinking:
samir: lean towards separate endpoint. Savedviews can store an inspector_ref (uuid) + snapshot_ts. Inspector service can materialize heavy telemetry on demand. Avoid bloating savedview objects.
liam: If separate, need a synchronous fallback for small customers who want immediate preview without an extra call. Maybe console does an async fetch and shows a loading skeleton, but on export we fetch materialized snapshot.
maya: UX prefers having inspector contents captured in the snapshot workflow for rollouts — so we can see historical routing choices. But agreed on keeping active fetch lightweight.
nina: Proposed minimal API shape (separate endpoint):
```
GET /api/inspector/{inspector_id}
Response 200 {
  "inspector_id": "uuid",
  "route_id": "route_x",
  "snapshot_ts": 1670000000,
  "mappings": [
    {"model_id":"m-gg-32","variant":"v2-q4","policy":"latency","quota_bucket":"gold","sampling_rate":0.1,"est_cpm":"$0.12"}
  ],
  "telemetry_refs": ["telemetry_stream_id"]
}
```
This keeps savedview small (inspector_ref) and inspector can keep heavier telemetry refs.
samir: +1. We should also add a small boolean `is_materialized` and a quick link to telemetry trace id for deep-dive.
liam: Implementation detail: console should call /inspector?route=...&ts=... to get the latest inspector_id if none exists, then call the inspector_id endpoint. That gives us caching and dedup.
maya: Rollout UX: when canary changes policy (e.g., route switches to cost-first), inspector should show a diff: prior_policy -> new_policy + delta in sampling/quota. Small UI affordance: `Show policy diff` button.
nina: Telemetry cost note: pulling full token-level telemetry for inspector materialization can be expensive. Suggest we store lightweight aggregates for the inspector (histograms for lat/lat-p95, token burn estimates) and link to full traces only on demand.
samir: Action items:
- samir: draft inspector API + schema (this week)
- nina: update Console mocks and skeletons (next sprint)
- liam: add feature flag + telemetry hooks for sampling/materialization (so infra can gate cost)
- maya: write short product doc for rollout UX and diffs
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Note: canary routing policies recorded by infra at tagging time. If you need a sample deployment to test inspector, open a deploy ticket with `deploy-bot create-sample`
liam: One more internal API question — persistence: inspector materializations should be TTL'd. Propose 90 days by default, configurable per-org. Thoughts?
maya: 90 days default sounds fine. Add admin console controls later.
nina: OK I'll prototype the endpoint shape and include `is_materialized`, `ttl_seconds`, `size_bytes` in the response so Console can show a warning when fetching large snapshots.
samir: Great. I'll start the API PR and ping infra for a cost guardrail on the materialize job.
maya: Thanks all. If there are no blockers I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow to align mocks + API. :thumbsup:
liam: ack.
ops-bot: reminder: weekly infra blackout window Thu 02:00-03:00 UTC — avoid long materialization runs then.
